{{Quote|No one enters Borkeen, that strip of shattered space debris; no one, for no one ever returned — save me.|Sosakar, from "The Slug Named Grendel" by Rogar Farnoster|<ref name="Sourcebook2">{{WEGCite|story=The Slug Named Grendel (short story)|book=The Star Wars Sourcebook (Second Edition)}}</ref>}}
The '''Borkeen Belt''', also known as the '''Borkeen asteroid belt''', was a dangerous [[Asteroid field/Legends|asteroid belt]] situated in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Belsmuth sector/Legends|Belsmuth sector]]. It was home to an eighty-[[Meter/Legends|meter]]-long [[Exogorth/Legends|exogorth]] that was discovered by [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] by [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] from the [[University of Sanbra]]. At some point after the [[Declaration of a New Order|formation]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the [[Author/Legends|author]] [[Rogar Farnoster]] wrote the [[Book/Legends|novel]] ''[[The Slug Named Grendel]]'', which mentioned both the Borkeen Belt and [[Grendel (space slug)|Grendel]], a giant exogorth living therein that was also the subject of a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] legend.

==Description==
{{Quote|The Borkeen asteroids are a roiling morass of stone and iron, flinders of a broken planet flung through the void. More ships have come to grief on those harsh rocks than mortals can count.|Sosakar, from "The Slug Named Grendel" by Rogar Farnoster|<ref name="Sourcebook2" />}}
The Borkeen Belt,<ref name="Sourcebook2" /> also referred to as the Borkeen asteroid belt<ref name="CSWE" /> or simply as Borkeen,<ref name="Sourcebook2" /> was an [[Asteroid field/Legends|asteroid belt]]<ref name="CSWE" /> located in the [[Belsmuth sector/Legends|Belsmuth sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="EAOC" /> It was an infamous [[Navigator/Legends|navigational]] hazard.<ref name="CSWE" /> In the [[Book/Legends|novel]] ''[[The Slug Named Grendel]]'' by [[Rogar Farnoster]], the Borkeen Belt was described as a dangerous collection of [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroids]] composed of [[Stone/Legends|rock]] and [[Iron/Legends|iron]] that were the remnants of a broken-up [[Planet/Legends|planet]].<ref name="Sourcebook2" /> An eighty-[[Meter/Legends|meter]]-long [[Exogorth/Legends|exogorth]] lived in the belt<ref name="HNN" /> in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].<ref name="Date">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|54|life/1352_2.html|Giant Space Slug Found}} is set on the [[Great ReSynchronization calendar|date]] "13:5:2," which corresponds to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] per the reasoning [[Template:YearMathGRS|here]].</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|Scientists have confirmed the existence of a 80-meter long space slug living within the Borkeen Belt in the Outer Rim Territories.|HoloNet News report|<ref name="HNN" />}}
[[File:SpaceSlug.jpg|thumb|right|300px|An eighty-meter-long exogorth (an exogorth pictured) was discovered in the Borkeen Belt.]]
According to a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] legend, the Borkeen Belt was home to [[Grendel (space slug)|Grendel]], a giant exogorth that preyed upon [[Starship/Legends|starships]] and had destroyed more than a thousand vessels.<ref name="Kids">{{Kids1997Cite|19|Who Is That Alien?|Who Is That Alien? Space Slugs & Mynocks}}</ref> [[Scientist/Legends|Scientists]] from the [[University of Sanbra]] at one point visited the asteroid belt, where they confirmed the existence of the largest exogorth the [[University/Legends|university]] had ever found. On the [[Great ReSynchronization calendar|date]] 13:5:2, the discovery was noted in a report from the Borkeen Belt published in an issue of the [[HoloNet News CoCo District Edition|CoCo District Edition]] of the [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]].<ref name="HNN" />

At some point after the [[Declaration of a New Order|reorganization]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]<ref name="Sourcebook2" /> into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the best-selling [[Author/Legends|author]] Rogar Farnoster, who had accompanied the scientists to the Borkeen Belt,<ref name="HNN" /> wrote<ref name="Sourcebook2" /> the novel<ref name="HNN" /> ''The Slug Named Grendel''. In the work's opening chapter, the character [[Sosakar]] described the Borkeen Belt and Grendel and recounted how they had joined the crew of the starship ''[[Darkfire]]'' of the [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] [[Flandon Sweeg]]&mdash;whose previous crew had abandoned him when he revealed his plan to venture into the belt in search of Grendel&mdash;and subsequently encountered the giant exogorth.<ref name="Sourcebook2" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Borkeen Belt was first mentioned in "[[The Slug Named Grendel (short story)|The Slug Named Grendel]]," a short companion narrative included in ''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]'', a [[1987]] sourcebook authored by [[Bill Slavicsek]] and [[Curtis Smith]] for use with [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="Sourcebook1">{{WEGCite|story=The Slug Named Grendel (short story)|book=The Star Wars Sourcebook}}</ref> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Borkeen [[Star system/Legends|system]], and therefore the Borkeen Belt, in grid square O-6.<ref name="TEA" />

"[[Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star, How I Wonder Where We Are]]," a [[1990]] [[roleplaying game]] source article published in the [[Voyages SF 13|thirteenth issue]] of the ''[[Voyages SF]]'' magazine, placed the Borkeen Belt in the [[Darpa sector/Legends|Ralltiir sector]].<ref name="Twinkle">{{VoyagesCite|13|Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star, How I Wonder Where We Are}}</ref> The article is considered [[Canon|noncanonical]] with respect to the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity.<ref name="Unlicensed">{{UnlicensedStatus}}</ref>
